data.narrative:
Svante, a Series E climate and energy technology company founded by Brett Henkel, has raised $318M to date. The comparable universe in Climate & Energy comprises one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers—only one adjacent-stage peer and zero same-stage peers met filtering criteria—rendering a traditional peer-median approach unreliable.

The analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, applying a 1.4x multiplier to the $318M total raised proxy to estimate the Series E post-money valuation. This step-up reflects typical capital efficiency and momentum between Series E and subsequent rounds in the sector. This method yields an implied valuation of $445M.

The triangulated valuation range is $378M (low), $445M (median), and $512M (high), derived from stage-progression anchoring with standard error bounds. The median of $445M represents the primary supported value. Key uncertainties stem from the narrow applicability of available methods—only one valuation approach could be reliably applied—and the absence of tightly comparable peers at the same stage and valuation tier. Resolution of these uncertainties would require additional market data on recent Series E and Series F financings in deep-tech climate solutions.
